name: NY-26
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Tim Kennedy running with $2.3M raised and $1.2M on hand
Challenger Dennis Hannon has no reported fundraising
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Kennedy: a Democratic-leaning district, incumbency, and a large financial edge against a challenger with no visible fundraising. Markets price Kennedy around 96%, consistent with a safe Democratic rating.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a single-digit race or unexpected outside spending against Kennedy would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Tim Kennedy, the Democratic incumbent, seeks re-election in a Buffalo-area district that leans Democratic by about 11 points. He has raised roughly $2.3 million and holds about $1.2 million on hand, while Republican challenger Dennis Hannon reports no fundraising. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets put Kennedy's chances near 96 percent.

The combination of district lean, incumbency, and a lopsided money advantage makes an upset unlikely. The forecast expects Kennedy to win comfortably, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of polling rather than any specific evidence of a competitive race.
